title: Things: a, an, the, this, these

sections.title: What you will learn to say

blocks.text: In this lesson you learn to name the things around you: «it's a chair», «they're tickets», «this charger», «those flowers are fresh», «the mistake is here», «it's a red cup». English uses small words in front of things for this: a, an, the, this, that.

examples.translation: The flowers over there are fresh.
One cup, and it is red.

sections.title: One thing: put a in front

blocks.text: Before one thing, English almost always puts a small a: It is a chair. a means «one», but it's very short and quiet. Without it the sentence sounds broken.

examples.translation: You're not sure it's a table.

blocks.text: In questions and with not, a stays in its place: Is it a table? It is not a window.

sections.title: a or an: the first sound decides

blocks.text: If the word starts with a vowel sound, say an instead of a: an armchair, an oven, an umbrella. It's easier to say: you don't get stuck between two vowel sounds.

examples.translation: You wear it on your ear.
A paper that says what to pay.

drill.why: umbrella starts with a vowel sound, so an.

blocks.text: Listen to the sound, not the letter. In hour the h is silent, so it starts with a vowel sound: an hour. But uniform and euro start with a «y» sound («you-niform», «you-ro»). That's not a vowel sound, so a.
Easy check: say the word out loud. Does it start with an «a, e, i, o, u» sound? Then an. A «y» sound or any other sound? Then a.

sections.title: More than one: add s, drop a

blocks.text: For more than one thing, add s: ticket → tickets. And drop a, because a means «one». The clip changes too: one thing — it is; more than one — they are.

drill.prompt: A courier gives you some tickets. Say what they are.

blocks.text: If the word ends in s, sh or ch, you can't just add s. Add es, and the word gets one more beat: bus → buses, dish → dishes, watch → watches. You can hear it: «bus-iz», «dish-iz».
If the word ends in y and there is a consonant before it, change y to ies: battery → batteries, city → cities. It sounds almost the same, with a soft «z» at the end.

examples.translation: Where is the book with the stories?

drill.why: There's a consonant (r) before y, so y becomes ies.

sections.title: this and that: near or far

blocks.text: Near you, in your hand — this. Far from you, something you point at — that. It's only about distance.

examples.translation: It's over there on the wall.
The thing over there is something else.

drill.question: The screen is on the far wall of the room. What do you say?
drill.explain: The screen is far away, so that.

sections.title: these and those: more than one

blocks.text: For more than one thing, this becomes these and that becomes those. The clip is are. Near — these are. Far — those are.

examples.translation: The shoes in front of me.
The sheets over there are big.

drill.why: More than one shoe, and they are near: these.

blocks.text: this, that, these and those can go right before a thing: this album, those flowers. Then you don't need a. One thing — this or that. More than one — these or those, and the word has s.

examples.translation: The album near me is big.
The frames near me cost little.
The flowers over there are fresh.
The building we are in is new.
Is the lemon near you ready to eat?

blocks.text: a is for something you mention for the first time, when the other person doesn't know which one yet: A cashier is here. the is for something you both already know about: The mistake is here.

examples.translation: There is someone at the till.

blocks.text: First a, then the: This is a mistake. — Where? — The mistake is here. Now you both know which one.

drill.why: You both know which mistake, so the.

sections.title: Things in general: no a, no the

blocks.text: When you talk about a kind of thing in general, not specific ones, just use the word with s: Books are heavy — any books. The magazines are new — these magazines that you both can see.

sections.title: Colour and other details go before the thing

blocks.text: The colour comes before the thing: a red cup, not a cup red. Colours never take s: black chairs, not blacks chairs. a or an depends on the first sound of the very next word: an olive coat, a yellow vase.

examples.translation: One cup, and it is red.
A coat the colour of olives.
The round table here is heavy.
The boxes made of metal are heavy.
The scarf with stripes is new.

drill.prompt: The seller asks which cup you want. Say it's a red cup.

blocks.text: Before you name a thing, ask two questions. One or more? One — a/an, this/that. More — s at the end, these/those, are. And: does the other person know which one? If yes — the.

drill.question: The shirts are in front of you. Which is correct?
drill.explain: More than one shirt, and they're near: these.

blocks.text: One thing — a or an by the first sound. More than one — add s, no a. Near — this / these; far — that / those. Something you both know — the. In general — no the. Colour before the thing: a red cup.

examples.translation: One cup, and it is red.
